Definition: from G40; to make holy, i.e. (ceremonially) purify or consecrate; (mentally) to venerate:--hallow, be holy, sanctify.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, hagiázō is the word for hallow, be holy, sanctify. In Matthew 6:9, the text says "Hallowed be thy name." In Luke 11:2, the text says "Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done."
TheologicalSignificance: What hagiázō teaches me is that purity is not prudishness; it is keeping ourselves for the God who made us. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
